answer: Sliding-window rate accrual resists sybils: influence accumulates only as fast as a fixed per-identity rate over a sliding time window, so no account can bank a burst — a thread of contribution earns weight only as real minutes pass. A swarm spun up across the tundra cannot fast-forward; each fake accrues at the same capped rate, and the mesa of total influence rises only with elapsed wall-clock, not head count. An attacker trades time, not accounts, and time cannot be parallelized across fakes.
